# Phantom command reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_command_reference.py. Do not edit. -->

Generated from the live shell registry, every module's `do_*` handlers,
the C2 shell and `phantom.main.build_parser()`. Regenerate with:

```bash
python scripts/generate_command_reference.py
```

The command column uses the hyphenated spelling the shells accept.
`help <command>` prints the same text shown here.

## Manual shell commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `save-profile` | save-profile <name> — save current settings as a profile. |
| `load-profile` | load-profile <name> — load a profile. |
| `list-profiles` | List all saved profiles. |
| `set` | set target <ip/domain/email> \| set scope <cidr,...> \| set lhost <ip> \| set lport <port> |
| `show` | show [session] \| show scope \| show mode \| show knowledge |
| `note` | note "<text>" — add an inline note to the session |
| `notes` | Display all notes in the current session |
| `save-session` | save-session <name> — save current session to disk |
| `load-session` | load-session <name> — load a previously saved session |
| `list-sessions` | List all saved sessions (manual .json + auto .pm bundles) |
| `export-session` | export-session [<file.pm>] — bundle this engagement into ONE portable .pm file (session + auto-mode checkpoint + report index) that another operator can open with import-session, or that resumes with `auto <target> --resume <checkpoint>`. |
| `import-session` | import-session <file.pm> — open a .pm bundle exported by another operator (or another machine): restores target/scope/notes/knowledge and stages the checkpoint for `auto <target> --resume <file>`. |
| `history` | Show command history for this session |
| `run` | run [n \| module [args]] — one step, from the ranked moves or a module. |
| `suggest` | suggest — ranked, directly executable next moves. |
| `plan` | plan <goal> — the reasoning engine lays out the chain to a goal. |
| `preflight` | preflight [module] — check the tools a module needs and show install hints for the missing ones. Without arguments checks the module you would run next. |
| `craft` | craft <ipgrab\|reel\|image\|pixel\|beacon\|kits\|hits\|wait> — build a social lure and get it ready to paste, then watch for the target. |
| `map` | map [cidr] — discover live hosts on the local network (or the given CIDR), feed the network map + WorldModel, then rank every device by reachable attack surface and suggest where to start. |
| `install` | install <tool> — install a missing tool in the current backend environment (apt / brew / choco / pip, auto-selected; WSL on Windows). Asks first and shows the exact command; `deps install` asks the same way. Then shows the live output. |
| `scan-diff` | scan-diff <target> [--since YYYY-MM-DD \| --old TS --new TS] |
| `use` | use <module> — enter a module (built-in or plugin; aliases: s, o, w, e, b, p, h, v, a, r, wl) |
| `plugins` | plugins — list all loaded plugins. |
| `auto` | auto \| auto <target[,target...\|CIDR]> [flags] - Autonomous kill chain. |
| `agent` | agent <target[,target...]> [--aggressive] [--goal <goal>] [--max-agents N] Autonomous agent campaign (one sub-agent per target). |
| `bench` | bench [list\|<scenario>] [--iterations N] [--json] - Offline auto-mode benchmark (ground truth + failure injection). |
| `c2` | c2 - Enter the Phantom C2 Operations Center |
| `malleable` | malleable [show\|save\|recommend] - Manage malleable C2 profiles for beacon stealth |
| `ad` | ad [tree\|paths\|add-user <u> [opts]\|add-edge <src> <type> <dst>\|reset] - BloodHound-style AD attack graph from session knowledge. |
| `wordlists` | wordlists list \| wordlists use <name> \| wordlists search <keyword> \| wordlists info <name> |
| `export` | export <json\|pdf\|html> [filename] — export session results |
| `guardrails` | guardrails [list\|enable <key>\|disable <key>\|why\|record] — safety controls |
| `deps` | deps [report\|install <tool>...] -- the external tools Phantom shells out to |
| `llm` | llm [journal [refusals] \| propose [n] \| proposals \| accept <id> \| reject <id> [reason] \| clear] |
| `social` | social [graph [--json\|--graphml FILE] [--run] \| emails <address> [--reset-only]] |
| `help` | help [command] — Show the help panel or details about a specific command. |
| `workflow` | workflow [show\|types\|next] [target-type] — inspect the LEGACY phase engine |
| `config` | config [status\|rotate-api-token\|keys\|dead-drop <url>\|dead-drop publish <host> <port>] - Operator state. |
| `tool` | tool list\|import <binary>\|approve <id>\|enable <id>\|disable <id> - Runtime tool drivers. |
| `setup` | setup [status\|auto] - Detect transports, configure optional channels interactively and write data/config.json (no .env editing needed). |
| `coverage` | coverage [profile] - Capability coverage audit. |
| `doctor` | doctor [--net] - Environmental self-check in one command. |
| `why` | why [capability] - Why did the agent do (or veto) that move? |
| `run-diff` | run-diff <checkpointA> <checkpointB> - Compare two runs structurally. |
| `experience` | experience [list [N] \| forget <N> \| forget all] - Learning memory. |
| `where` | where - Print the current layer, target and scope in one line. |
| `back` | Return to main shell (already here) |
| `exit` | exit - Exit Phantom, optionally save current session and generate professional report |
| `quit` | exit - Exit Phantom, optionally save current session and generate professional report |

## Common module commands

Available inside every `use <module>` session.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `back` | Return to the main shell |
| `exit` | Exit Phantom |
| `help` | List available commands or show detailed help. |
| `note` | note "<text>" — add an inline note to the current session. |
| `preview` | preview — REVIEW the command plan without executing anything. `run` executes (interactive selection), `preview` only shows. |
| `quiet` | quiet — toggle non-interactive mode (top suggestion, raw output). |
| `run-group` | run-group <name> — execute exactly ONE group of this module's plan. |
| `run` | run [--quiet] — EXECUTE the module flow (interactive selection). `preview` only shows the plan; `run` executes it. With --quiet: execute the top suggested command directly (pipe-able). |
| `show` | Show session - current session |
| `suggest` | suggest — show state-aware commands for the current session. |
| `where` | where - Print the current layer, target and scope (same as the shell) |

## Module-specific commands

### `scan`

_No module-specific commands; use `suggest`, `run` or `preview`._

### `osint`

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `cookies` | cookies [domain ...] — read THIS box's browser sessions locally (Chrome/Edge DPAPI, no beacon, no config) for OSINT authed views. Values stay in the WorldModel under the standard protections; only domains + counts are shown here and stored in results. |
| `crtsh` | crtsh — manual lookup of subdomains via crt.sh. |
| `diff` | diff <session1> <session2> - Compare OSINT results between two saved sessions. |
| `phone` | phone — phone-number OSINT: carrier + region via phonenumbers (offline, never the subscriber's identity). Writes an `identity` finding to the shared knowledge. |
| `set-key` | set-key <key> - Save Shodan API key (session AND config plane, so it survives a restart without editing .env). |
| `sherlock` | sherlock [username] - Search social media for a username. |
| `shodan` | shodan <query> - Execute a Shodan search (Key required in session config). |

### `wifi`

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `airmon` | airmon <start\|stop\|check> [interface] - Manage monitor mode. |
| `crack` | crack <cap_file> [wordlist] - Crack WPA/WPA2 handshake with aircrack-ng. |
| `deauth` | deauth <bssid> [count] - Send deauthentication frames to disconnect clients. |
| `handshake` | handshake <bssid> <channel> - Targeted handshake capture with auto-deauth. |
| `pmkid` | pmkid <bssid> <channel> - Capture PMKID hash (clientless WPA attack). |
| `scan-aps` | scan-aps - Scan for Access Points using airodump-ng. |

### `web`

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `creds` | creds — extract credentials from web services (SSRF → credential files, SQLi auth-bypass + UNION dump + MD5 hash-crack). The SAME deterministic engine the auto-mode agent uses, run interactively. Found pairs are written to the shared WorldModel where the exploit / pivot modules can reuse them. |
| `dirsearch` | dirsearch <wordlist> — Fast directory brute-force. |
| `hunt` | hunt — behavioural bug-class hunting (baseline + statistical anomaly scoring + validation pass): the SAME anomaly engine the auto-mode agent runs, executed interactively with real requests. Confirmed candidates are written to the shared WorldModel, where the reasoning engine can turn them into rce_foothold hypotheses. |
| `nikto` | nikto — Smarter Nikto wrapper with result parsing. |
| `sqlmap` | sqlmap <target_url> — Smarter SQLmap wrapper with --batch. |
| `whatweb` | whatweb — Fingerprint web technologies. |

### `brute`

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `crack` | Crack password hashes with John the Ripper or Hashcat. |
| `defaults` | defaults [service] — try the known DEFAULT credentials for a service first (fast, quiet, the senior move before any noise): routers, cameras, NAS, appliances. Found pairs are written to the shared knowledge (usable by payload/pivot and the report). |
| `run` | Interactive wizard for network brute force. |

### `exploit`

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `chain` | chain [plan\|go <n>] — Search the composition engine for attack paths from the facts Phantom already holds (SSRF -> cloud keys, upload -> webshell -> RCE, SQLi -> creds -> SSH...). Shows every step with cost/noise; executes only what you approve. |
| `deploy-agent` | deploy-agent [windows\|linux\|macos\|android] — Compile beacon and get C2 dropper one-liner. |
| `execute` | execute <name> — Launch a dynamic exploit by script name. |
| `fire` | fire <cve_id> [--port N] [--msf] [--poc] [--command CMD] — Execute the real weapon for one CVE through the trusted execution bridge. |
| `list-exploits` | list-exploits — Show available dynamic exploit scripts. |
| `msf-fire` | msf-fire <cve_id> [--port N] — Force Metasploit execution. |
| `msf-interact` | msf-interact <id> — interactive loop against a live MSF session (stays alive in msfrpcd after you detach). |
| `msf-status` | msf-status — list live Metasploit sessions (persistent RPC). |
| `poc-sync` | poc-sync [term\|cve:CVE-XXXX-NNNNN] — Mirror real PoC scripts for the detected services (or an explicit search term) from the local ExploitDB copy via searchsploit, tag them with METADATA and file them under exploits/pocs/ so 'fire' can run them directly. |
| `privesc-run` | privesc-run — actively enumerate privilege-escalation vectors on the target over SSH (sudo -l, SUID binaries, writable passwd/shadow, GTFOBins hints). Differs from 'privesc' (payload module) which only lists tools: this runs the real enumeration and stores findings. |
| `remote-deploy` | remote-deploy [windows\|linux\|macos] — Compile the standalone Remote Session module and print the dropper one-liner. |
| `run` | Build and execute the best access path from scan results. |
| `ssh` | ssh [user:pass] — open an SSH session to the target using a credential pair from the shared WorldModel (or an explicit user:pass). Picks the SSH port the scanner discovered (incl. non- standard). This is how creds found via 'use web' → 'creds' become actual access on the box. |

### `payload`

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `bind` | bind [port] — synthesize a BIND shell (target listens). LOUD BY NATURE: only use when outbound egress is blocked. |
| `deploy` | deploy — build and preflight PHANTOM's OWN C++ beacon dropper for the detected target platform (the same binary the auto-mode ships), then print the one-liner to execute on the target. |
| `generate` | Interactive payload generation wizard with auto OS/arch detection. |
| `hid` | hid <board> ["<command>" \| --from-payload <id> \| --stager <os>] [flags] |
| `privesc` | privesc — run ACTIVE privilege-escalation enumeration on the target (sudo -l, SUID, writable files) using harvested creds, and list the matching GTFOBins/tools. Falls back to the tool list when no access is available yet. |
| `reverse` | reverse [lhost] [lport] — synthesize a multi-dialect reverse shell with the enterprise payload engine (the same one the auto-mode ships): best dialect for the target platform, optional base64 encoder, automatic listener, and the beacon upgrade path. |
| `run` | run [--quiet] — EXECUTE the module flow (interactive selection). `preview` only shows the plan; `run` executes it. With --quiet: execute the top suggested command directly (pipe-able). |

| Command | What it does |

| `run` | run [--quiet] — EXECUTE the module flow (interactive selection). `preview` only shows the plan; `run` executes it. With --quiet: execute the top suggested command directly (pipe-able). |

## AUTO-MODE flags (`phantom --auto <target> ...`)

| Flag | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--profile` | Load engagement profile at startup (manual shell) |
| `--c2` | Launch Phantom C2 interface instead of the AUTO-MODE shell |
| `--manual` | Launch the MANUAL module shell instead of AUTO-MODE (the module workflow is also a `manual` mode inside the AUTO shell) |
| `--auto` | AUTO-MODE: with target(s) run the full kill chain directly; with no target open the interactive AUTO-MODE shell (same as `phantom.auto`) |
| `--stealth` | paranoid OPSEC (auto-mode) |
| `--aggressive` | loud, fast exploitation (auto-mode) |
| `--speed` | exploit first viable opening (auto-mode) |
| `--exploit-all` | auto-mode: after the normal run, consider every CVE/web/service access candidate but EXECUTE only the best path (plus one fallback); a verified RCE is then used to deliver the beacon |
| `--exhaustive` | auto-mode LAB/DEBUG only: try every actionable access candidate instead of the best path; noisy and not for real engagements |
| `--reason` | auto-mode REASONING objective: balanced (default), stealth_first (buy quiet), evidence_first (buy information), force_first (only sane with --aggressive) |
| `--identity-active` | auto-mode DEDICATED consent for ACTIVE identity probes (reset enumeration, SMTP email verify); separate from --aggressive |
| `--cell-loop` | auto-mode CELL LOOP (always on): the cell roster is the AUTHORITY for every goal; the flag is accepted for compatibility |
| `--cell-stages` | auto-mode: constrain the roster to these GOALS (comma-separated, e.g. deliver,post_exploit; trialling only — the roster stays the authority) |
| `--oM` / `--only-markdown` | auto-mode LEARNING MODE: draft markdown proposals in docs/evolution/ instead of authoring code (no LLM, no lab; separate daily budget) |
| `--plan` | dry-run: show plan, execute nothing (auto-mode) |
| `--verbose` | stream live reasoning trace (auto-mode) |
| `-a` / `--agents` | sub-agent count: -a (auto) or -a2 (auto-mode) |
| `--goal` | terminal goal (auto-mode, default: deliver) |
| `--profile-auto` | target profile (auto-mode, default: enterprise) |
| `--resume` | resume from an auto-mode checkpoint (auto-mode) |
| `--resume-latest` | resume the NEWEST auto-mode checkpoint with nobody watching (unattended restart, bounded by a persisted counter so a crash loop terminates) |
| `--supervise` | auto-mode: keep the run alive WITHOUT anybody watching — a crash mid-engagement relaunches it from its checkpoint, and so does a run that ended cleanly WITHOUT reaching its goal (`completed` != goal reached); both are bounded by the same persisted counter, and Ctrl+C is a stop, never a relaunch |
| `--max-restarts` | auto-mode --supervise: automatic relaunches allowed after a crash (default 3; 0 refuses every unattended restart) |
| `--print-service` | auto-mode: print the OS service definition for THIS invocation to stdout (nothing is written) — review it, or redirect it into the unit path |
| `--install-service` | auto-mode: WRITE the service definition that starts this run after a reboot (it is not enabled: the command to enable it is printed) |
| `--uninstall-service` | auto-mode: remove the service definition (--service-name selects which one) |
| `--service-name` | auto-mode service definition: unit name (default: one per platform) |
| `--service-system` | auto-mode service definition: a system-level unit instead of a per-user one (needs root to enable; survives a logout) |
| `--llm` | optional local-LLM advisor (auto-mode) |
| `--ai` | AI layer mode (auto-mode): off (default), local llama.cpp, cloud OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or integrated promoted per-phase adapter; per-phase overrides live in ai.<phase>.mode |
| `--ai-authority` | AI authority override (auto-mode): auto (default) lets the measured eval gate decide. nudge/decide/full FORCE a level and say so in the run log — an override is announced, never silent, and it can never make a model add candidates or emit commands |
| `--experience` | CROSS-ENGAGEMENT learning memory (auto-mode): keep cause->repair experience between runs (default: learning is scoped to this run only) |
| `--evolution` | SELF-IMPROVEMENT (auto-mode): stable uncovered failure patterns spawn a background sub-agent that authors a new capability and opens a reviewable PR (lab required; max 2 PRs/day) |
| `--beta` | BETA CAPABILITIES (auto-mode): fetch open auto-evolution PRs, gate them locally and use the ones that pass (same full gate, lab included; working tree untouched) |
| `-y` / `--yes` | Run mode sequences without confirmation prompts |
| `--setup` | guided setup: 'wsl' for the Windows WSL toolbox flow, none for the full wizard (tools, doctor) |
| `--doctor` | diagnostics only: python, tools, docker, WSL, LLM transport — installs nothing |

## C2 shell commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `audit` | audit [verify\|tail N] - inspect the immutable C2 audit log. |
| `autopersist` | autopersist - Automatically attempt persistence based on OS detection. |
| `back` | back - return to main C2 shell from interaction mode |
| `beacon-auth` | beacon-auth <status\|rotate\|revoke> [beacon_id] - Manage beacon identity keys. |
| `beacon-help` | beacon-help - list commands supported by the C++ beacon agent |
| `beacons` | beacons - list active beacons with real-time status |
| `certs` | certs [status\|uninstall] - Inspect or remove the TLS certificate pair. |
| `config` | config (status\|rotate-api-token\|mtls-on\|mtls-off) - Show/rotate auto-generated C2 secrets. |
| `exit` | exit - Close C2 and return to main Phantom CLI (or exit completely) |
| `generate` | generate [windows\|linux\|macos\|android] [x64\|x86] [--profile <json>] - Generate beacon and dropper |
| `generate-shellcode` | generate_shellcode [platform] - Generate Base64 shellcode for inject/migrate. |
| `health` | health - Beacon health self-report: uptime, check-in ok/fail counters, tasks done, current sleep/jitter cadence, build id. |
| `help` | help [command] - Show the C2 command reference for the current context |
| `inject` | inject <pid> - Inject beacon into a remote process. |
| `interact` | interact <beacon_id> - drop into beacon interaction mode (prefix match supported) |
| `keylog` | keylog <start\|stop\|status\|dump> - Manage keylogger instance (Windows only) |
| `listeners` | listeners [start <port> [host] [use_ssl]] \| stop] - Manage C2 listener. |
| `malleable` | malleable [show\|save\|recommend] - Manage malleable C2 profiles |
| `mem-run` | mem-run <b64_shellcode> - Execute shellcode in memory (Windows/Linux). |
| `migrate` | migrate [pid] - Migrate beacon into a new process. |
| `payloads` | payloads [id] - list compiled payload droppers (optionally show one by id) |
| `persist` | persist [runkey\|schtask\|cron\|systemd] - Generate and queue a persistence task for the active beacon. |
| `quit` | - |
| `remote-expire` | remote-expire <seconds\|now> — Set the remote session lifetime (P0-7): the module stops accepting input and streaming when the deadline passes; 'now' revokes the running session immediately. The task is audited in the immutable log. |
| `remote-open` | remote-open — open the most recent full-resolution remote frame in the OS image viewer (Ghost workspace at native quality). |
| `remote-view` | remote-view [gui\|off] — Watch the Remote Session module's stream. |
| `results` | results [n\|all] - show results for the active beacon (default last 10) |
| `screen-open` | screen-open [name] — open a saved screen recording (mp4) in the OS video player. Without a name, opens the newest recording. |
| `screen-watch` | screen-watch [gui] — Watch beacon screen recordings. |
| `screenshot` | screenshot - Capture a screenshot of the target (Windows only) |
| `set-sleep` | set-sleep <ms> [jitter%] - Rotate the beacon cadence mid-session (no restart, no redeploy). The beacon applies it at the next check-in. |
| `telegram` | telegram — Start the Telegram bot to manage beacons from mobile |
| `tunnel` | tunnel [start [port]\|install\|stop] - Public hop for delivery (c2.front). |
| `unpersist` | unpersist [name] - Remove the persistence the beacon installed. |
| `where` | where - Print the current layer, target and scope (same as the shell) |
